key_insight: A scalable Bayesian Gaussian process classifier improved prediction and uncertainty calibration in breast cancer histopathology benchmarks, with the largest gains under hospital-level distribution shift.
clinical_relevance: Better-calibrated uncertainty could support more reliable cross-hospital pathology AI, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Uses frozen Phikon pathology foundation model embeddings.
Applies accelerated RPCholesky for low-rank kernel approximation.
Combines non-centered Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling with pivot-based inducing points for prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on PCam and CAMELYON17-WILDS with training scale around 300,000 samples, the method reduced expected calibration error by up to 88% and false negative rate by up to 90% versus variational GP and neural network baselines.
watch_item: Benchmark results do not establish clinical readiness; prospective cross-site validation and assessment of sampling costs are still needed.
paper_title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
